system.name: Pruner
system.one_liner: a draft-then-verify exploration mechanism that accelerates tensor program tuning using a fast draft model and a learned cost model

components.name: Deep Neural Networks
components.role: input DNN, converted into partitioned small subgraphs using a graph partitioning algorithm

components.name: Tuning Scheduler
components.role: schedules tuning of subgraphs over multiple rounds using Ansor's gradient-based task scheduler

components.name: Graph Partition
components.role: partitions the DNN into small subgraphs using a graph partitioning algorithm

components.name: Gradient-based Task Scheduler
components.role: selects one subgraph per round according to the tuning record; adopted from Ansor

components.name: Draft: Latent Schedule Explorer
components.role: the 'Draft' component (LSE) that designs hardware-aware symbols/penalties to roughly estimate performance for rapid exploration

components.name: Hardware-aware Symbols
components.role: hardware-aware symbols and penalties describing utilization of hardware performance across memory levels

components.name: Symbol-based Analyzer
components.role: naive draft model used to draft small-scale potential candidates

components.name: Verify: Pattern-aware Cost Model
components.role: the 'Verify' component (PaCM) that applies a learned cost model to identify the best drafted candidates

components.name: Temporal Dataflow Pattern
components.role: pattern-aware cost model sub-component modeling temporal dataflow patterns

components.name: Pattern-aware Transformer
components.role: pattern-aware cost model sub-component; a transformer-based learned cost model

components.name: Momentum online Adaptation
components.role: MoA-Pruner's momentum-based online adaptation strategy addressing cross-platform online unawareness; activated only for MoA-Pruner in online tuning

components.name: Optimal Tensor Program
components.role: final tuned output of the search process

flows.what: DNN partitioned into subgraphs and scheduled for tuning
drafted candidates passed to the cost model for verification
verified candidates feed into momentum online adaptation
feedback loop for online cost-model tuning back into the task scheduler

content.key_idea: Pruner accelerates tensor program tuning with a draft-then-verify loop: a lightweight Latent Schedule Explorer drafts candidates, a Pattern-aware Cost Model verifies them, and MoA-Pruner's momentum online adaptation feeds results back into the scheduler.
content.reading_order: top-down through the stacked stages from DNN input to Tuning Scheduler, Draft, Verify, Momentum online Adaptation, and the Optimal Tensor Program, with a feedback arrow to the scheduler

summary: Figure 2 is Pruner's system overview, drawn as a top-down pipeline of color-coded stage bands, each labeled with its paper section. Deep Neural Networks (Sec 3) are partitioned via Graph Partition and scheduled by Ansor's Gradient-based Task Scheduler inside the Tuning Scheduler. Schedule Generation feeds the Draft stage, Latent Schedule Explorer (LSE, Sec 4.1), whose Hardware-aware Symbols and Symbol-based Analyzer roughly estimate performance to draft candidates; a red arrow marks these Drafted candidates flowing into the Verify stage, Pattern-aware Cost Model (PaCM, Sec 4.2), built from a Temporal Dataflow Pattern and Pattern-aware Transformer. Momentum online Adaptation (Sec 4.3, MoA-Pruner only) then produces the Optimal Tensor Program and loops feedback back up to the Tuning Scheduler for online cost-model tuning. Peach, brown, blue, green, yellow and gray bands distinguish input, scheduling, draft, verify, adaptation, and output stages respectively.
